title: The constant coefficient objects are bounded constructible
statement:
Fix the finite-field datum [def-weil-finite-field-fiber] $p,a,q,k_0,k$, a prime $\ell\neq p$, an algebraic closure $\Qlb$ of $\Ql=\mathbf Q_\ell$, a finite extension $E/\Ql$ contained in $\Qlb$ with valuation ring $\mathcal O_E$ and uniformizer $\varpi_E$, and for $n\geq1$ put $A_{E,n}=\mathcal O_E/\varpi_E^n$. Let $Y$ be a scheme, with small pro-etale site $Y_{\mathrm{proet}}$ [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site]; let $(A_{E,n})_Y$ be the constant sheaf of the ring $A_{E,n}$ on $Y_{\mathrm{proet}}$ (the sheafification of the constant presheaf, as in that definition), and let $\widehat{\mathcal O}_{E,Y}=\varprojlim_n(A_{E,n})_Y$ be the completed integral coefficient sheaf [def-weil-completed-integral-coefficients]. Then:

1. $(A_{E,n})_Y$, placed in degree $0$, is an object of $D^b_c(Y,A_{E,n})$ [def-weil-finite-torsion-constructibility]: it is locally constant on the single stratum $Y$ with finite stalks $A_{E,n}$.
2. $\widehat{\mathcal O}_{E,Y}$, placed in degree $0$, is an object of $D^b_c(Y,\mathcal O_E)$ [def-weil-derived-complete-integral-detailed]: it is derived complete [def-weil-derived-complete], the canonical map $\widehat{\mathcal O}_{E,Y}\otimes^L_{\mathcal O_E}A_{E,n}\to(A_{E,n})_Y$ (the derived reduction modulo $\varpi_E^n$ [def-weil-integral-derived-reduction]) is an isomorphism for every $n\geq1$, and the cohomological supports [def-weil-cohomological-support] of these reductions are all contained in $[0,0]$.
3. Consequently $E_Y$, the image of $\widehat{\mathcal O}_{E,Y}$ in the rationalized category $D^b_c(Y,E)=D^b_c(Y,\mathcal O_E)[1/\varpi_E]$ [def-weil-rationalization-karoubi], and $(\Qlb)_Y=(E,E_Y)$ in the common-stage category $D^b_c(Y,\Qlb)$ [def-weil-algebraically-closed-coefficients], are objects of those categories, and $(\Qlb)_Y$ is independent of the stage $E$: for finite extensions $E\subset L$ in $\Qlb$, the integral scalar extension [def-weil-integral-scalar-extension] gives an isomorphism $\widehat{\mathcal O}_{E,Y}\otimes_{\mathcal O_E}\mathcal O_L\cong\widehat{\mathcal O}_{L,Y}$ in $D(Y_{\mathrm{proet}},\mathcal O_L)$, hence $E_Y\otimes_EL\cong L_Y$ in $D^b_c(Y,L)$, and its class is an isomorphism $(E,E_Y)\cong(L,L_Y)$ in $D^b_c(Y,\Qlb)$.

source.place: node def-weil-ordinary-compact-cohomology, order 1510: 'let $\Lambda_Y$ denote its coefficient object on the small pro-etale site ... Abbreviate $H^i(Y,\Lambda)=H^i(Y,\Lambda_Y)$' (for $H^i(Y,\Lambda_Y)$ to be defined, $\Lambda_Y$ must be an object of $D^b_c(Y,\Lambda)$; the blueprint does not say so). The integral case is Bhatt-Scholze, literature/bhatt-scholze-pro-etale-topology_arXiv-1309.1198.pdf, Definition 6.8.1 and Lemma 6.8.2(1) ($\mathcal O_{E,X}=\widehat{\mathcal O}_E=\varprojlim_n\mathcal O_E/\varpi^n$)

proof.text: Finiteness and the tower. By [lem-weil-valued-dvr-finite-quotients] (applied to $\mathcal O_E$, a discrete valuation ring with finite residue field by [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]), each $A_{E,n}$ is a finite ring and each reduction $A_{E,n+1}\to A_{E,n}$ is surjective. Hence the morphism of constant sheaves $(A_{E,n+1})_Y\to(A_{E,n})_Y$ is surjective: every section of $(A_{E,n})_Y$ over $U$ is, on the members of some covering of $U$, a constant section $a\in A_{E,n}$ (sheafification [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site]), and $a$ lifts to $A_{E,n+1}$.

source.place: p. 49, §6.5, first paragraph (the sheaves $R/\mathfrak m^n$ on $X_{\mathrm{proet}}$ and $\widehat R=\lim R/\mathfrak m^n$, here $R=\mathcal O_E$, $\mathfrak m=(\varpi_E)$); p. 58, Lemma 6.8.2(1)

proof.text: Part 1. Take the partition of $Y$ with the single stratum $Y_1=Y$ ($N=1$), with immersion $i_1=\mathrm{id}_Y$. The set $Y$ is open and closed in $Y$, hence locally closed, and constructible (it is open and retrocompact in $Y$) [def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties]. The restriction $\mathrm{id}_Y^*(A_{E,n})_Y$ is $(A_{E,n})_Y$ itself (inverse image along the identity), and it is constant, hence locally constant (take the one-member covering $\{\mathrm{id}:Y\to Y\}$ of $Y_{\mathrm{proet}}$) [def-weil-proetale-locally-constant-sheaf]. Its stalk at every geometric point of $Y$ [def-weil-proetale-geometric-stalk] is $A_{E,n}$ by [lem-weil-proetale-constant-sheaf-stalk], a finite $A_{E,n}$-module by Step 1. So $(A_{E,n})_Y$ is a constructible sheaf of $A_{E,n}$-modules [def-weil-proetale-constructible-sheaf].

source.place: p. 49, §6.5, paragraph after Definition 6.5.1 ($D_{cons}(X_{\mathrm{proet}},R/\mathfrak m^n)\simeq D_{cons}(X_{\mathrm{et}},R/\mathfrak m^n)$; the constant sheaf $R/\mathfrak m^n$ is the pullback of a constant, hence constructible, etale sheaf); the stratification and stalks are written out here

proof.text: The complex $(A_{E,n})_Y[0]$ has $\mathcal H^0=(A_{E,n})_Y$ and $\mathcal H^i=0$ for $i\neq0$ [def-weil-derived-cohomology-sheaves]: finitely many nonzero cohomology sheaves, all constructible by Step 2. Hence $(A_{E,n})_Y\in D^b_c(Y,A_{E,n})$ [def-weil-finite-torsion-constructibility], and its cohomological support [def-weil-cohomological-support] is contained in $\{0\}$ (it is $\{0\}$ if $Y\neq\emptyset$ and empty if $Y=\emptyset$). This proves Part 1.

Reductions of $\widehat{\mathcal O}_{E,Y}$. The one-term complex $P=\widehat{\mathcal O}_{E,Y}$ in degree $0$ is K-flat over $\widehat{\mathcal O}_{E,Y}$: for every acyclic complex $M$ of $\widehat{\mathcal O}_{E,Y}$-modules, $\widehat{\mathcal O}_{E,Y}\otimes_{\widehat{\mathcal O}_{E,Y}}M\cong M$ termwise (unit isomorphism of the tensor product of sheaves of modules [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product]), which is acyclic. So the identity $P\to\widehat{\mathcal O}_{E,Y}$ may be used in [def-weil-integral-derived-reduction], and $\widehat{\mathcal O}_{E,Y}\otimes^L_{\mathcal O_E}A_{E,n}=\widehat{\mathcal O}_{E,Y}\otimes_{\widehat{\mathcal O}_{E,Y}}(A_{E,n})_Y\cong(A_{E,n})_Y$, the isomorphism being the unit isomorphism; this is the canonical map of Part 2, which is therefore an isomorphism. Under these isomorphisms the transition maps of the system $(\operatorname{Res}_n(\widehat{\mathcal O}_{E,Y}\otimes^L_{\mathcal O_E}A_{E,n}))_n$ of [def-weil-derived-complete] are the reduction maps $\operatorname{Res}_{n+1}(A_{E,n+1})_Y\to\operatorname{Res}_n(A_{E,n})_Y$, and the maps $\widehat{\mathcal O}_{E,Y}\to\operatorname{Res}_n(A_{E,n})_Y$ are the limit projections $\pi_n$ [def-weil-completed-integral-coefficients] (the unit isomorphism is natural in the second factor).

source.place: p. 24, Definition 3.5.2 (the maps $\widehat R\to R/\mathfrak m^n$ and $K\otimes^L_{\widehat R}R/\mathfrak m^n$); p. 49, Lemma 6.5.4 and the notation of §6.5 ('when $L=R$ or $R/\mathfrak m^n$ we drop the underline')

proof.text: By Step 4 and Part 1, every reduction $\widehat{\mathcal O}_{E,Y}\otimes^L_{\mathcal O_E}A_{E,n}\cong(A_{E,n})_Y$ lies in $D^b_c(Y,A_{E,n})$, and their cohomological supports are all contained in the single interval $[0,0]$, independent of $n$ (Step 3).

$\widehat{\mathcal O}_{E,Y}$ is derived complete. The $\widehat{\mathcal O}_{E,Y}$-modules $F_n=\operatorname{Res}_n(A_{E,n})_Y$ form an inverse system with surjective transition maps (Step 1; $\operatorname{Res}_n$ does not change the underlying sheaf), and their limit in sheaves of $\widehat{\mathcal O}_{E,Y}$-modules is $\widehat{\mathcal O}_{E,Y}$ itself with projections $\pi_n$ (limits of sheaves of modules and of rings are computed on the underlying sheaves [def-pur-sheaf-inverse-limit, def-weil-completed-integral-coefficients]). By [lem-weil-proetale-surjective-tower-derived-limit] (clause 2), with $\mathcal R=\widehat{\mathcal O}_{E,Y}$, $\widehat{\mathcal O}_{E,Y}$ in degree $0$ is a derived limit $R\varprojlim_n\operatorname{Res}_n(A_{E,n})_Y$ in $D(Y_{\mathrm{proet}},\mathcal O_E)$ [def-weil-derived-limit]; by clause 3, the canonical map $\widehat{\mathcal O}_{E,Y}\to R\varprojlim_n\operatorname{Res}_n(A_{E,n})_Y$ of [def-weil-derived-complete], which is the map compatible with the $\pi_n$ of Step 4, is the unique such map, namely the identity of $\widehat{\mathcal O}_{E,Y}=\varprojlim_n(A_{E,n})_Y$, an isomorphism. Hence $\widehat{\mathcal O}_{E,Y}$ is derived complete [def-weil-derived-complete].

source.place: p. 17, Proposition 3.1.10 ($\lim F_n\simeq R\lim F_n$ for surjective towers in a replete topos), with p. 18, Proposition 3.2.3(1) and p. 29, Proposition 4.2.8; p. 24, Definition 3.5.2 ($m$-adic completeness of $K\in D(X,\widehat R)$)

proof.text: Part 2. By Steps 4, 5 and 6, $\widehat{\mathcal O}_{E,Y}$ is derived complete, its reductions lie in $D^b_c(Y,A_{E,n})$ and have cohomological supports in $[0,0]$ for every $n$; so it is an object of $D^b_c(Y,\mathcal O_E)$ [def-weil-derived-complete-integral-detailed].

source.place: p. 49, Definition 6.5.1 (here $K\otimes^L_{\widehat R}R/\mathfrak m=(A_{E,1})_Y$ is the pullback of the constant etale sheaf, so $\widehat R\in D_{cons}(X_{\mathrm{proet}},\widehat R)$); p. 58, Lemma 6.8.2(1) ($\mathcal O_{E,X}=\widehat{\mathcal O}_E$)

proof.text: Part 3, objects. The rationalized category $D^b_c(Y,E)=D^b_c(Y,\mathcal O_E)[1/\varpi_E]$ has the same objects as $D^b_c(Y,\mathcal O_E)$ [def-weil-rationalization-karoubi], so $E_Y$, the object $\widehat{\mathcal O}_{E,Y}$ of Part 2 viewed there, is an object of $D^b_c(Y,E)$. The objects of $D^b_c(Y,\Qlb)=\mathcal C_Y$ are the pairs $(E,K)$ with $E\in\mathcal E_\ell$ and $K\in D^b_c(Y,E)$ [def-weil-algebraically-closed-coefficients], so $(\Qlb)_Y=(E,E_Y)$ is one.

source.place: p. 58, Lemma 6.8.2(2) ($E_X=\mathcal O_{E,X}[\ell^{-1}]$) and Definition 6.8.1; the categories here are those of the DAG, not Bhatt-Scholze's

proof.text: Integral scalar extension of $\widehat{\mathcal O}_{E,Y}$. Let $E\subset L$ be finite extensions of $\Ql$ in $\Qlb$, $e$ the ramification index, so $\varpi_E\mathcal O_L=\varpi_L^e\mathcal O_L$. As in Step 4 the K-flat representative $P=\widehat{\mathcal O}_{E,Y}$ gives $\widehat{\mathcal O}_{E,Y}\otimes^L_{\mathcal O_E}A_{L,m}=\widehat{\mathcal O}_{E,Y}\otimes_{\widehat{\mathcal O}_{E,Y}}(A_{L,m})_Y\cong(A_{L,m})_Y$ [def-weil-integral-scalar-extension, def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product], with the reductions $(A_{L,m+1})_Y\to(A_{L,m})_Y$ as transition maps; these are surjective by Step 1 applied to $L$. Their limit is $\widehat{\mathcal O}_{L,Y}$ [def-weil-completed-integral-coefficients for $L$], so by [lem-weil-proetale-surjective-tower-derived-limit] (with $\mathcal R=\widehat{\mathcal O}_{L,Y}$) $\widehat{\mathcal O}_{E,Y}\otimes_{\mathcal O_E}\mathcal O_L=R\varprojlim_m\operatorname{Res}_m(A_{L,m})_Y\cong\widehat{\mathcal O}_{L,Y}$ in $D(Y_{\mathrm{proet}},\mathcal O_L)$, the isomorphism being compatible with the projections to the $(A_{L,m})_Y$.

source.place: agent-written; the analogue in the source is p. 58, Lemma 6.8.2(1)-(2) and its proof on p. 59 ($\mathcal O_{E,X}$ is $\varprojlim_n\mathcal O_E/\varpi^n$ for every finite $E$, and $\mathcal O_{E,X}=\operatorname{colim}_F\mathcal O_{F,X}$)

proof.text: Independence of the stage. The scalar-extension functor $-\otimes_EL:D^b_c(Y,E)\to D^b_c(Y,L)$ is, on objects, $K\mapsto K\otimes_{\mathcal O_E}\mathcal O_L$, the integral scalar extension of an integral representative, viewed in the rationalization [def-weil-rationalization-karoubi]. On the representative $\widehat{\mathcal O}_{E,Y}$ of $E_Y$, Step 9 gives an isomorphism $\phi:\widehat{\mathcal O}_{E,Y}\otimes_{\mathcal O_E}\mathcal O_L\cong\widehat{\mathcal O}_{L,Y}$ in $D(Y_{\mathrm{proet}},\mathcal O_L)$, between objects of the full subcategory $D^b_c(Y,\mathcal O_L)$ (Part 2 for $L$), and Step 9 with $E=L$ gives $\psi:\widehat{\mathcal O}_{L,Y}\otimes_{\mathcal O_L}\mathcal O_L\cong\widehat{\mathcal O}_{L,Y}$; their images in $D^b_c(Y,L)$ are isomorphisms $\phi:E_Y\otimes_EL\cong L_Y$ and $\psi:L_Y\otimes_LL\cong L_Y$ (a functor carries isomorphisms to isomorphisms). So $u=\psi^{-1}\phi:E_Y\otimes_EL\to L_Y\otimes_LL$ represents a morphism $[L,u]:(E,E_Y)\to(L,L_Y)$ of $\mathcal C_Y$, and $[L,u^{-1}]$ a morphism back; their composites are represented over $L$ by $u^{-1}u$ and $uu^{-1}$, identities, which represent the identities of $(E,E_Y)$ and $(L,L_Y)$. Hence $[L,u]$ is an isomorphism $(E,E_Y)\cong(L,L_Y)$ in $D^b_c(Y,\Qlb)$ [def-weil-algebraically-closed-coefficients]. This proves Part 3.

split_report.summary: Wrote a 10-step proof following Bhatt-Scholze §6.5, Definition 3.5.2, Proposition 3.1.10 and Lemma 6.8.2(1): (A_{E,n})_Y is constructible on the single stratum Y with stalks A_{E,n}; the one-term complex Ohat_{E,Y} is K-flat, so its reductions are the constant sheaves (A_{E,n})_Y; derived completeness is the surjective-tower case of R lim = lim on the replete pro-etale topos; Part 3 (stage independence) is agent-written via the integral scalar extension node and the same tower lemma. Step 2 uses def-weil-proetale-locally-constant-sheaf and def-weil-proetale-geometric-stalk, created today by the worker of def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties. Created two unsplit nodes: lem-weil-proetale-constant-sheaf-stalk (stalks of constant sheaves at geometric points) and lem-weil-proetale-surjective-tower-derived-limit (BS Prop. 3.1.10 in the form of a Roos triangle, with uniqueness of the induced map). Statement: the reduction is now cited as def-weil-integral-derived-reduction (the notion def-weil-derived-complete-integral-detailed uses) instead of def-weil-derived-tensor, and the stage-independence clause of Part 3 is made precise through def-weil-integral-scalar-extension; stmt_deps updated accordingly (added def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension, def-weil-algebraic-closure, def-weil-integral-derived-reduction, def-weil-integral-scalar-extension; removed def-weil-derived-tensor).
